title: OPTIMJACK: Optimizely-Hosted Scripts Loaded a Crypto Clipper and Card Skimmer
content_md: According to Report URI [2], malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organizations through the Optimizely Web Experimentation platform on November 16, 2026, including several high-profile organizations. The malicious code was injected into the Project JavaScript field of customer projects and subsequently served through Optimizely’s legitimate CDN. The payload was capable of replacing cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled addresses, stealing payment-card information, accessible cookies and screenshots, and delivering additional malicious payloads to iPhones and iPads [2]. Affected Products Optimizely Web Experimentation Exploitation According to Report URI [2], malicious JavaScript was identified in 188 infected Optimizely snippets associated with 178 organizations. The malware replaced cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled addresses, and Report URI observed verified cryptocurrency transactions to the attackers. According to StepSecurity [3], public scan records showed requests to the malicious infrastructure from affected websites between 08:28 and 21:23 UTC on November 16, 2026.
